Effects of a measured intervention on service reliability

Alex Researcher

Roles: Conceptualization, Methodology, Writing

Affiliation Reliability Research Centre

Taylor Analyst

Roles: Data curation, Formal analysis, Review

Affiliation Systems Engineering Institute

The study compares the intervention with a control group across six months.

The measured result shows a clear reduction in failed requests.

The evaluation uses the same request mix, deployment schedule, and observability rules for both groups. This keeps the comparison stable across the study period.

Engineers reviewed the measurements after each release and recorded the reasons for every observed failure. The review found no material change in traffic shape.

The result remains consistent when the analysis excludes short-lived incidents and when it uses the median rather than the mean recovery time.

These findings support the conclusion that the intervention improves service reliability under the tested operating conditions.
